title: Cap. VIII: Calvin Institutes — guilt follows hereditary corruption
pass_a_gloss: Calvin states his mind elsewhere. Original sin, he says, is our nature's wickedness and corruption. First it makes us liable to God's anger; then it also produces in us the works Scripture names works of the flesh. So guilt follows corruption as an effect follows its cause — and follows it as what they call an adequate cause. He adds at once: two points must be kept distinct — we are ruined and twisted in every part of our nature, and for that corruption alone we already stand rightly condemned and convicted before God. Those same words pleased him so much that they appear twice in the Institutes: book 2, chapter 1, section 8, and book 4, chapter 15, section 10.
pass_b_english: Elsewhere Calvin unfolds his mind. "Original sin," he says, "is the depravity and corruption of our nature, which first makes us guilty of the wrath of God, then also brings forth in us works which Scripture calls works of the flesh" (Galatians 5:19). Therefore guilt follows corruption as effect follows cause — and indeed, as they say, an adequate cause: for he subjoins at once. "These two things, then, are to be observed distinctly: namely that, being thus spoiled and perverted in all the parts of our nature, we are already held before God justly damned and convicted on account of that corruption alone." Which same words so pleased so great a man that they stand twice in his Institutes — once in book 2, chapter 1, section 8, and again in book 4, chapter 15, section 10.
source_text: Exponit mentem suam alibi Calvinus, Peccatum originale, inquit, est naturae nostrae pravitas ac corruptio, quae primum reos facit nos irae Dei, tum etiam opera in nobis profert quae Scriptura vocat opera carnis. Sequitur ergo reatus corruptionem ut effectus causam, & quidem causam, ut loquuntur, adaequatam: subiungit enim continuo. Haec itaque duo distincte observanda: nempe quod sic omnibus naturae nostrae partibus vitiati perversique, iam ob talem duntaxat corruptionem damnati merito convictique coram Deo tenemur. Quae eadem verba, adeo tanto viro placebant, bis extant in ejus institutione, semel lib. 2. cap. 1. §. 8. & iterum lib. 4. cap. 15. §. 10.
